walkthroughs.body_html:
Gas Exchange & Respiration — a core area of GCSE Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Gas Exchange & Respiration brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Gas Exchange & Respiration.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

A series of chemical reactions in cells that break down glucose to release energy as ATP.
Anaerobic respiration produces oxygen as a waste product.
Plants only photosynthesise and do not respire; respiration is for animals only.
Plants only respire at night and only photosynthesise during the day; the processes never overlap.
Yes — plants respire all the time to release energy; they also photosynthesise when there is light.

mcqs.q: What is produced in anaerobic respiration in human muscle cells?
options: Lactic acid (lactate) and a small amount of ATP — no CO2 or water in this pathway.
Respiration is the process by which plants make their own food using sunlight.

Anaerobic respiration produces oxygen as a waste product.

mcqs.q: Lungs have about 500 million alveoli. Total surface area is about 70 m². Estimate area per alveolus in 10⁻⁷ m².
Exhaled air contains more carbon dioxide and water vapour than inhaled air. Which process in the body's cells explains this?
options: Aerobic respiration
Photosynthesis
Digestion
Breathing alone, with no chemical reaction

mcqs.q: Alveoli have a very large surface area and walls only one cell thick. How does this help gas exchange?
options: It increases the rate of diffusion of gases.
It slows diffusion to protect the lungs.
It allows active transport of oxygen.
It stops carbon dioxide leaving the blood.

mcqs.q: When the diaphragm contracts and flattens, what happens to volume and pressure in the chest, and which way does air move?
options: Volume increases, pressure falls, air moves in
Volume decreases, pressure rises, air moves in
Volume increases, pressure rises, air moves out
Volume decreases, pressure falls, air moves out

mcqs.q: Limewater turns cloudy faster when a student breathes out through it after exercise than at rest. Which conclusion is supported?
options: More CO₂ is produced because respiration has increased.
The lungs produce less CO₂ during exercise.
Exercise stops the body from respiring.
The limewater reacts with oxygen, not CO₂.
